About

An analyst who starts with the business

I have spent five years working close to the business, not at a distance from it. At Deloitte I produced financial reporting that stakeholders relied on cycle after cycle. At Infosys I built the pipelines behind reporting for two clients — Takeda in healthcare and Resolution Life in insurance — across policy, claims, and premium data loaded into Snowflake. At Quest Global I support a financial services client where my reporting feeds receivables, payments, and collections decisions.

That experience shapes how I work. I begin with the decision a report has to support, then clean and model ERP, policy, claims, and finance data so the numbers tie back to source — and present them so a busy manager gets the answer in seconds.

I am focused on Data Analytics Engineer, Data Analyst, BI Analyst, and Reporting Analyst roles where Power BI, SQL, and Microsoft Fabric are central.

01 — ANALYTICS ENGINEERINGgithub.com / financial-services-analytics-platform

Financial Services Analytics Platform

Daily, trusted visibility into accounts, transactions, and exceptions.

The problem: raw financial extracts arrive messy — mixed date formats, duplicate events, and the same metric defined differently in every report. Finance teams cannot act on numbers they do not trust.

The build: a production-style pipeline on synthetic financial services data, with layered bronze, silver, and gold contracts and one governed set of reporting tables, so every metric is defined once and checked before it is used.

  • Star schema with customer, account, date, and transaction dimensions
  • SQL validation for uniqueness, referential integrity, nulls, and business rules, with pytest coverage
  • Portable by design to Microsoft Fabric, Snowflake, Databricks, or SQL Server
What it proves

Analytics engineering done properly: governed data, tested logic, and reporting a finance team can rely on every day.

PythonSQLDimensional ModelingData Qualitypytest

Inside the repository

  • Python ingestion and transformation pipeline with bronze, silver, and gold layer contracts.
  • Star schema so metric logic lives once in the gold layer, not copied across reports.
  • Validation checks and tests documented alongside the code. Synthetic data only — no employer or customer data.

02 — AI WORKFLOWGitHub

No-Code Claims Intake Agent

Unstructured claim requests, turned into structured, traceable work.

The problem: claims arrive as free text with missing details, so intake teams spend their time chasing information instead of resolving cases. Drawn directly from my insurance reporting work at Infosys.

  • Structured intake through Copilot Studio conversation topics
  • Power Automate routing by confidence and urgency, with human handoff for low-confidence or high-risk requests
  • Case records and audit events, with Power BI operations metrics
What it proves

Responsible AI workflow design: the agent clarifies, classifies, and routes — it never approves or denies a claim. A human stays in charge.

Copilot StudioPower AutomateGovernancePower BI

Inside the blueprint

  • Conversation topics that clarify missing details before a case is created.

03 — POWER BIGitHub

DAXWELL Power BI Sales Analysis

Which categories and regions drive profit — and where discounts stop helping.

The problem: sales volume alone hides the real story. This report separates revenue from profit, so a business can see where growth is healthy and where discounting is quietly eating margin.

  • Executive overview: KPI cards, monthly trend, sales by category, profit by region
  • Discount analysis: discount bands and a discount versus profit scatter
  • Customer insights: new versus repeat customers, top 10 customers, monthly active customers
Key takeaway

Discounts can support sales, but strategy has to stay balanced with margin — and repeat customers provide stable long-term value.

04 — MICROSOFT FABRIC · POWER BINew · Portfolio build

Receivables & Collections Analytics in Microsoft Fabric

One trusted view of what is owed, what is overdue, and where collections effort should go next.

The problem: this is the reporting problem from my day job at Quest Global, rebuilt as a standalone portfolio build. Finance teams working from separate ERP extracts cannot see aging, overdue risk, or payment behaviour in one place — so follow-up effort goes to the loudest account, not the riskiest one.

  • Fabric Lakehouse on OneLake with bronze, silver, and gold layers, fed by Dataflows Gen2 and pipelines
  • Power BI semantic model with DAX measures for aging buckets, DSO, overdue share, and collection effectiveness
  • Customer risk view ranking accounts by overdue balance and days past due, so collections follow-up is prioritised by risk
What it proves

End-to-end Fabric analytics — ingestion, modelling, governed DAX measures, and a finance-ready dashboard. The exact stack behind my DP-700 certification and my Quest Global reporting work.

Microsoft FabricPower BIDAXOneLakeT-SQLDataflows Gen2

Inside the build

  • Lakehouse tables for invoices, payments, and customers, modelled into a star schema for the gold layer.
  • Aging calculated as of the reporting date, not stored as static buckets, so the view is correct for any day it is opened.
  • Built on synthetic ERP-style data only — no employer or customer data.

05 — HEALTHCARE ANALYTICS · SNOWFLAKE · POWER BINew · Portfolio build

Healthcare Claims Analytics in Snowflake & Power BI

Where are claims denied, where is payment stuck, and which providers need attention first?

The problem: this is the reporting problem from my healthcare work at Infosys for Takeda, rebuilt as a standalone portfolio build. Policy, claims, and premium data arrive from different sources, so denial patterns, payment delays, and provider variation stay hidden until someone pulls the data together by hand.

  • Snowflake fact and dimension model for claims, policy, member, and provider data, so every report uses the same governed definitions
  • SQL transformations and ETL pipeline logic in the style of my Informatica IICS work, with data quality and reconciliation checks before release
  • Power BI semantic model with DAX measures for denial rate, paid vs billed, average days to pay, and claims by type and provider
What it proves

Healthcare analytics engineering end to end — validated Snowflake modelling, reconciled claims and premium reporting, and Power BI that payer and provider stakeholders can trust cycle after cycle.

SnowflakePower BIDAXSQLInformatica IICSHealthcare ClaimsData Validation

Inside the build

  • Claims fact table joined to policy, member, provider, and date dimensions, with denial reason as a tracked, reportable field — not buried in notes.
  • Denial analysis by reason, provider, and claim type, so operations can fix the top causes first instead of working denials one by one.
  • Built on synthetic healthcare-style data only — no Takeda, employer, member, or patient data.
